backups.replicateDescription: Sends the backup files to a backup pool of a remote cluster. The copy there is an ordinary backup that can be restored on that cluster. An incremental backup is sent with the earlier backups of its chain that the remote cluster does not have yet, starting from the full backup. Deleting this backup deletes the copy too.

backups.name: Name (optional)

backups.incrementalHint: Copies only the blocks changed since the last backup of this VM in the pool. A full backup is taken when that is not possible, such as when the VM is stopped or has no earlier backup there.
backups.busy: The VM is starting, stopping or migrating. Back it up when it has settled.
backups.restoreDescription: Makes a new stopped VM from the backup with copies of its disks. It gets new MAC addresses and the same networks and security groups.
backups.deleteDescription: The backup files are removed from the backup pool, and the copies sent to remote clusters are deleted too. This cannot be undone.

backupJobs.pageHint: Back up the chosen VMs at a set time and delete old backups by the retention rules. Times are in UTC. The cluster leader runs the jobs, at most a few backups per node at a time.
backupJobs.runRequested: {{name}} starts at the scheduler's next check.

backupJobs.retentionHint: Keeps the newest backups (Last), then the newest backup of each day, ISO week and month, counted per VM. Leave all at 0 to keep every backup. Failed backups are deleted after a later success.
backupJobs.fullEveryHint: With 0, every backup is full. With n, backups are incremental where possible and the backup after n incremental ones is full. For example, daily with 6 makes one full and six incremental backups a week.
backupJobs.replicateHint: Each backup the job makes is copied to this backup pool of the remote cluster. Failed copies are tried again at the next run.
backupJobs.deleteDescription: The job stops running. The backups it made are kept.

pools.createDescription: Where volumes are kept: a directory on each node, an NFS export that the nodes mount, an LVM thin pool or ZFS dataset on each node, a Ceph RBD pool, or a volume group shared by the nodes.

kindHint.dir: Create the directory on each node first.
kindHint.nfs: Each node mounts the export under its data directory. Mounting needs Linux nodes running as root. The pool is shared by its nodes.
kindHint.lvm-thin: Create the volume group and thin pool on each node first. Volumes are raw thin volumes kept on the node that creates them, and their snapshots hold disks only. Needs Linux nodes running as root.
kindHint.zfs: Create the dataset on each node first. Volumes are raw zvols kept on the node that creates them, and their snapshots hold disks only. Disks can only revert to their latest snapshot. Needs Linux nodes running as root.
kindHint.rbd: Create the Ceph pool first and put ceph.conf and the keyring on each node. Volumes are raw RBD images that every node of the pool can use, and their snapshots hold disks only. Needs Linux nodes with QEMU's rbd driver (qemu-block-extra) and the rbd command (ceph-common).
kindHint.lvm-shared: Create the shared volume group (vgcreate --shared) on a LUN every node sees first, and run lvmlockd with sanlock or dlm on each node. Volumes are raw logical volumes that every node of the pool can use, without snapshots. Needs Linux nodes running as root.

pools.exportHint: The absolute path the server exports, such as /srv/vm.
pools.optionsHint: Comma-separated options passed to mount -o after nosuid,nodev,noexec,retry=0, such as vers=4.2,hard.

errors.export: Enter an absolute path (starting with /) without control characters.

errors.options: Separate the options with commas, without spaces. bind, rbind, remount, move, suid, dev, exec, helper, bg and x-* options are not allowed.
errors.lvmName: Use 1 to 127 letters, digits, +, _, . or -, not starting with -, snapshot or pvmove. LVM also reserves . and .. and names containing parts like _tdata or _tmeta.
errors.zfsDataset: Use a dataset name such as tank/opl, at most 177 characters: parts separated by / with letters, digits, _, ., : or -, none empty, . or .. or starting with -. The pool name comes first and starts with a letter.
errors.rbdName: Use 1 to 63 letters, digits, _, . or -, not starting with -.
errors.cephUser: Write the Ceph user without the "client." prefix, for example opl instead of client.opl.
errors.rbdConf: Enter an absolute path (starting with /) without control characters, commas, colons or equals signs.
errors.portal: Enter a host name or IP address with an optional :port (1–65535), without spaces, commas or slashes. Put IPv6 addresses in brackets, such as [fd00::5]:3260.
errors.target: Use a target name starting with iqn., eui. or naa., at most 223 characters of lowercase letters, digits, ., : or -.

pools.portalHint: Host name or IP address with an optional port, such as san.lan:3260 or [fd00::5]:3260.
pools.targetHint: The target name, such as iqn.2003-01.org.example:storage.

kindHint.vxlan: orbivisord creates the bridge oplv<VNI> and a VXLAN device on every node and links them over UDP 4789.

networks.mtuHint: 1280–9000. Defaults to 1450: a 1500-byte underlay minus the 50-byte VXLAN header.
networks.userNote: The user network (QEMU NAT) is always available and is not listed.
networks.createDescription: Points VM interfaces at a Linux bridge on the nodes or at a VXLAN network that spans the nodes.

errors.reserved: The name user is reserved for NAT.

securityGroups.note: Firewall rules for VM interfaces. Nodes with nftables apply them right away, also to running VMs.
securityGroups.inUse: Remove it from the VM interfaces first.
securityGroups.createDescription: Creates an empty group. Add its rules on the next page.
securityGroups.deleteDescription: No VM interface uses it, so no traffic changes.
securityGroups.order: Rules are checked from the top, and the first match decides. An interface with groups drops incoming traffic that no rule accepts and sends outgoing traffic that no rule drops. With several groups, the first group's rules come first.
securityGroups.always: Always allowed: replies to allowed traffic, ARP, IPv6 neighbor discovery and DHCP replies. A VM can only send from its own MAC address.
securityGroups.noRules: No rules: incoming traffic is dropped and outgoing traffic is sent.

errors.ports: Use a port like 22 or a range like 8000-8080 (1–65535).
errors.icmpRemote: ICMP rules take only IPv4 addresses.
errors.icmpv6Remote: ICMPv6 rules take only IPv6 addresses.

drain.title: Drain {{name}}?
drain.description: The node enters maintenance, and its running VMs are live-migrated one at a time to other nodes the scheduler picks. The node stays in maintenance when the drain finishes or fails.
drain.localNote: VMs with disks on node-local pools are moved by copying their disks to a node with a pool of the same name (VMs with snapshots cannot be moved).

reason.hvf: VMs on a macOS node cannot be moved.

drain.endDescription: Ending maintenance stops the running drain.

nodes.removeDescription: Only for a node that is dead for good. It cannot rejoin with its current data, and VMs assigned to it stay assigned.
nodes.removeNote: Only offline nodes can be removed here. To remove a live node, run orbivisorctl cluster leave on it.

reason.thisNode: You are connected through this node.
reason.online: The node is online. Run orbivisorctl cluster leave on it.

updates.title: Updates for {{name}}
updates.truncated: Only the first {{count}} packages are shown.
updates.upgradeDescription: VMs keep running, but orbivisord restarts briefly. Upgrade other nodes after this upgrade finishes.

nodes.labelsDescription: Placement rules choose nodes by label (node_tag), such as zone=rack-a. The zone label follows [node] zone in the node's configuration.
nodes.labelsHint: KEY=VALUE pairs separated by commas. Leave empty to remove all.

errors.labels: Use KEY=VALUE pairs separated by commas.
errors.labelsChanged: The labels of this node changed elsewhere. Close this dialog and open it again.

unfreeze.title: Unfreeze {{name}}?
unfreeze.description: The node turned its HA VMs off for a host reboot, so HA waits for it to come back. If it will not come back, unfreeze it: the leader then recovers its HA VMs on other nodes as for a failed node.
unfreeze.done: {{name}} unfrozen. Its HA VMs are recovered on other nodes.

errors.node_online: The node is online again; it clears the mark itself.

fence.title: Power-off fencing of {{name}}
fence.description: When the node stops renewing its lease, the leader powers it off with these methods, in order, and recovers its HA VMs without waiting for the watchdog. If every method fails, it waits as before.
fence.none: No methods. The leader waits for the watchdog before recovering.
fence.note: The leader powers nodes off, and neighbour nodes (regular checks), the testing node and the leader read the power, so every node must reach the BMC. IPMI needs ipmitool on every node. Commands get ORBIVISOR_NODE_NAME, ORBIVISOR_NODE_ID and ORBIVISOR_NODE_ADDRESS.
fence.passwordSaved: A password is saved. Leave empty to keep it.
fence.systemIdHint: Empty: the only system of the BMC.
fence.insecure: Do not verify the BMC certificate
fence.offHint: Runs with /bin/sh -c on the leader. A non-zero exit fails.
fence.statusHint: Prints off or on on its first line. Runs on neighbour nodes, the testing node and the leader.
fence.checkedBy: Read by {{name}}. The power was not changed.

errors.no_fence_checker: No other online node can read this node's power. Test it from another node.
errors.fence_check_failed: The neighbour node did not answer: {{message}}

interfaces.open: Network interfaces and health checks of {{name}}: {{state}}
interfaces.title: Network interfaces of {{name}}
interfaces.description: What the node reports: the interface list every 30 seconds, link and bond state every 5 seconds. Bond ports that are not up are shown in red.
interfaces.none: The node reports no interfaces (witness nodes and macOS nodes do not).

portState.lacp_mismatch: LACP mismatch (not in the active aggregator or no partner)

interfaces.noChecks: The node reports no health checks.

nodes.replicasOpen: Show the {{count}} VMs {{name}} holds replicas of

disks.title: Disks of {{name}}
disks.description: Whole disks on the node and whether a Ceph OSD can use them. Disks in use (system, mounted, swap, ZFS, RAID, storage pool volume groups) are never erased.

accounts.changePasswordDescription: All your sessions end. Sign in again with the new password.
accounts.passwordChanged: Your password was changed. Sign in with the new password.

users.roleHint: Operators change VMs and volumes. Viewers only read. Neither can see accounts.
users.passwordDescription: The user's sessions end and they sign in with the new password.
users.deleteDescription: The user and their API tokens are deleted.
users.selfNote: Change your own password from the account menu. Only another administrator can change your role or delete your account.

reason.selfRole: Only another administrator can change your role.
reason.selfPassword: Change your own password from the account menu.
reason.selfDelete: Only another administrator can delete your account.

realms.pageHint: Users of a realm sign in with their directory (LDAP) or identity provider (OIDC) account as <name>@<realm>. Their role comes from their groups at each sign-in.
realms.empty: No realms. Only local users can sign in.
realms.displayHint: Shown on the sign-in page. Leave empty to show the name.
realms.urlHint: ldap:// always uses StartTLS. ldaps:// uses TLS from the start.
realms.bindDnHint: Service account used to find users. Leave empty to search anonymously.
realms.bindPasswordSaved: A password is saved. Leave this empty to keep it.
realms.userFilterHint: {username} is replaced with the escaped sign-in name.
realms.caPemHint: Trust only this CA for the directory's certificate. Leave empty to use the system roots.
realms.groupsHint: Group DNs match without regard to case. A user in several groups gets the highest role.
realms.formDescription: The role is set again from the mapping each time a user signs in.
realms.deleteDescription: Users of this realm can no longer sign in, and their sessions and API tokens stop working. The users stay; creating a realm with the same name lets them in again.
realms.testDescription: Checks each step of signing in as a directory user. No user or session is created.
realms.noRole: No role: sign-in would be refused.

errors.local: local is reserved for local users.
errors.taken: A realm with this name already exists.
errors.bindDn: Enter a bind DN to use a bind password.
errors.bindPasswordNeeded: Enter a bind password for the bind DN, or clear the bind DN to search anonymously.
errors.bindPasswordAgain: Enter the bind password again: the URL, bind DN or CA certificate changed.
errors.clearNeedsNoBindDn: To clear the saved password, also clear the bind DN.
errors.clearSaved: The bind DN is empty: choose "Clear the saved password" to search anonymously.
errors.timeout: Use a whole number of seconds from 1 to 30.
errors.group: Enter a group DN or remove the row.
errors.issuer: Use https://host[:port][/path] without a query or fragment.
errors.clientSecretAgain: Enter the client secret again: the issuer, client ID or CA certificate changed.

realms.issuerHint: https:// URL exactly as the identity provider reports it, including any trailing slash.
realms.clientSecretHint: Leave empty for a public client (PKCE only).
realms.clientSecretSaved: A secret is saved. Leave this empty to keep it.
realms.scopesHint: Separated by spaces. openid is required.
realms.groupsClaimHint: Claim with the user's groups as a list of strings.
realms.redirectUriHint: Register this address with the identity provider. Each node address you sign in through needs its own. Behind a reverse proxy, register the address the proxy passes as the Host.
realms.oidcCaPemHint: Trust only this CA for the identity provider's certificate. Leave empty to use the system roots.
realms.oidcGroupsHint: Group values from the groups claim match without regard to case. A user in several groups gets the highest role.
realms.oidcTestDescription: Checks the identity provider's discovery document and signing keys. No one signs in.

tokens.note: Scripts and tools use API tokens. A token has the role of its owner. orbivisorctl login makes one for the CLI.
tokens.createDescription: The token acts as you, with your role.
tokens.secretDescription: Copy the token now. It cannot be shown again.
tokens.deleteDescription: Anything using the token stops working right away.

cluster.title: Cluster {{name}}
cluster.caNote: Every node's HTTPS certificate is signed by the cluster CA. Import the CA into your browser to stop the certificate warning, and check that its fingerprint matches. Browsers show the SHA-256 fingerprint in uppercase hex, in pairs separated by colons or spaces; compare it with the hex after sha256: (letter case does not matter).
cluster.membersNote: Voters keep the cluster state. A learner is a standby or joining node with the full Raft log. An observer follows a voter outside Raft, so it adds no work to the leader. A witness votes but runs no VMs.
cluster.issueDescription: A new node joins with the token once. Start orbivisord on the new node first.
cluster.issuedDescription: Run this on the new node before {{time}}. It cannot be shown again.
cluster.commandNote: Add --socket if orbivisord on the new node does not use /run/opl/opld.sock.

remotes.pageHint: Other Orbivisor clusters this cluster can see. The status is collected every 30 seconds. What you can do on a remote cluster also depends on the role of the user who owns its API token there.
remotes.addDescription: Register another Orbivisor cluster with its address, the fingerprint of its CA and an API token created on it.
remotes.urlHint: https://host[:port] of a node of the remote cluster.
remotes.confirmFingerprint: This matches the CA fingerprint on the Cluster page of the remote cluster.
remotes.tokenHint: Create it on the API tokens page of the remote cluster. Its user's role there limits what this cluster can do.
remotes.tokenSaved: A token is saved. Leave this empty to keep it.
remotes.deleteDescription: This cluster stops showing it. Nothing changes on the remote cluster, and its API token stays there until you delete it.

errors.probeFirst: Get the CA of this URL first.
errors.confirm: Check the fingerprint against the remote cluster and confirm it.
errors.token: Enter an API token of the remote cluster.
errors.tokenAgain: Enter the API token again: the URL or CA changed.

vmForm.runningNote: The VM is running: its node, disks, and the number, order and MAC addresses of its interfaces cannot change, and if an interface has security groups, only the groups of the interfaces can change. Security groups apply right away; other changes apply from the next start.
vmForm.nicsRunning: Interfaces cannot be added or removed, and their MAC addresses cannot change, while the VM is running.
vmForm.noSecurityGroups: No security groups. Create them on the Security groups page.

errors.name: Use 1–63 lowercase letters, digits and -, not starting or ending with -.
errors.bootOrder: Boot orders must be unique numbers from 1 to 255.
errors.volumeDuplicate: Each disk needs a different volume.
errors.volumeExists: A volume with this name already exists.
errors.macMulticast: A multicast address (odd first byte) cannot be used.
errors.macDuplicate: Each interface needs a different MAC address.
errors.maxVcpusSockets: Must be a multiple of the number of sockets.
errors.memoryAlign: With a maximum, memory and maximum memory must be multiples of 128 MiB.
errors.replicationSnapshots: Replication cannot be used together with scheduled snapshots. Turn the snapshot schedule off.
errors.replicationDuplicate: This node is already a target.
errors.replicationOwnNode: The VM's own node cannot hold its replica.
errors.sataPorts: q35 has 6 SATA ports for SATA disks, CD-ROM drives and the cloud-init drive together.
errors.bootOverflow: The boot order leaves no room for the CD-ROM drives after it.
errors.ciHostname: Use a host name or FQDN: letters, digits and - in labels of up to 63 characters.
errors.ciRoot: Use SSH keys with the default user instead of root.
errors.ciUser: Use 1–32 lowercase letters, digits, _ and -, starting with a letter or _.
errors.ciIpv4None: Without IPv6 the NIC needs IPv4.
errors.ciPasswordHash: cloud-init cannot use yescrypt ($y$) or bcrypt-2b ($2b$) hashes. Use a SHA-512 crypt hash ($6$, e.g. mkpasswd -m sha-512) or a plain password.
errors.ciKey: Line {{n}} is not an SSH public key.
errors.ciKeysSize: The SSH keys are longer than 16 KiB together.
errors.ciAddress: Use an address with a prefix length, such as 10.0.0.5/24.
errors.ciGateway: Use an address of the same family.

vmForm.scheduleNote: Takes snapshots periodically and keeps only the newest scheduled ones. Snapshots you take yourself are never deleted. All disks must be qcow2, all in LVM-thin pools, all in ZFS pools, or all in Ceph RBD pools.
vmForm.scheduleRaw: {{volume}} is {{format}}, so scheduled snapshots will fail. All disks must be qcow2, all in LVM-thin pools, all in ZFS pools, or all in Ceph RBD pools.
vmForm.scheduleMemoryHint: Memory is saved only while the VM is running and has disks.
vmForm.scheduleMixed: Disks with different snapshot methods (qcow2, LVM-thin pools, ZFS pools, Ceph RBD pools) are mixed, so scheduled snapshots will fail.
vmForm.scheduleSharedLvm: {{volume}} is in a shared LVM pool, so scheduled snapshots will fail.
vmForm.haHint: Runs only on nodes with fencing on. If its node loses the cluster majority, the node stops the VM.
vmForm.haNodeOff: {{node}} has fencing off and cannot run HA VMs.
vmForm.haNoNode: No node has fencing on, so HA VMs cannot run.
vmForm.haRunning: Turn on HA while the VM is stopped.

haStateHint.started: If its node fails, HA starts the VM on another node.
haStateHint.stopped: If its node fails, HA moves the VM to another node but leaves it off.
haStateHint.ignored: HA leaves the VM alone for now: no fencing, recovery or counting. The settings are kept.

vmForm.haGroupHint: Recovers on the group's nodes, higher priority first.
vmForm.maxRestartHint: From 0 to 10 within 10 minutes. After that, HA moves the VM to another node.
vmForm.maxRelocateHint: From 0 to 10 within 10 minutes. After that, HA stops the VM and shows an error; start it again to clear it.
vmForm.haPriorityHint: From 0 to 100. When a node fails, HA restarts VMs with higher priority first.
vmForm.guestWatchHint: Pings the QEMU guest agent (qemu-guest-agent must run in the guest). Once it has answered, no answer for the time below force-restarts the VM. After a guest reboot it waits until the agent answers again. Can be turned on or off only while the VM is stopped.
vmForm.pinnedHint: The balancer never moves this VM. HA recovery, node draining and migrations you start still move it.
vmForm.maxVcpusHint: Leave empty for none. While running, vCPU cores can grow up to this on x86_64 nodes. Takes effect from the next start.
vmForm.maxMemoryHint: Leave empty for none. While running, memory can grow up to this on Linux nodes with virtio-mem. Takes effect from the next start.
vmForm.liveHint: vCPU cores and memory within the maximums apply right away where the node supports it. Other CPU, memory, firmware and machine changes apply at the next restart.
vmForm.runningNoteLive: The VM is running and its node cannot change. Hardware changes are applied while it runs where possible; the rest are listed on its page and apply at the next restart.
vmForm.restartForHotplug: The VM was started without hotplug support. Restart it once to add or remove disks and interfaces while it runs.
vmForm.disksLive: While the VM runs, volumes can be attached at the end (virtio-blk only, 8 devices at most) and disks attached while it runs can be removed from the end. Disks it started with cannot change.
vmForm.nicsLive: While the VM runs, interfaces can be added at the end (8 devices at most) and interfaces added while it runs can be removed from the end. The network, model and MAC address of a running interface cannot change; its security groups can.
vmForm.replicationNote: Only disks on node-local pools are replicated · Cannot be used together with snapshots. Copies the disks to each target node on a schedule; HA restarts the VM there from the latest copy if its node fails.
vmForm.haNoReplica: This VM cannot be restarted on another node: disk {{volume}} is on node-local pool {{pool}} and has no replica. Add replication.
vmForm.cdromsLive: While the VM runs, only the media can be changed (the drive tray is opened by force). Stop the VM to add or remove drives.
vmForm.bootOrderNote: The firmware tries the devices from the top. By default the disks come first and then the CD-ROM drives, so an empty disk boots the installer and the installed system boots afterwards.
vmForm.bootOrderRunning: Stop the VM to change the boot order.
vmForm.ciNote: Orbivisor attaches a NoCloud seed drive (label cidata). Cloud images and cloudbase-init read it at first boot.
vmForm.ciRunning: Changes apply at the next start of the VM (restart). A reboot inside the guest still sees the old settings.
vmForm.ciHostnameHint: Empty uses the VM name ({{name}}). A FQDN also sets the domain.
vmForm.ciUserHint: Renames the distribution's default user. Empty keeps its name.
vmForm.ciPasswordHint: Stored only as a SHA-512 crypt hash. A crypt hash ($6$…) is kept as it is. Empty means no password; SSH keys are safer.
vmForm.ciKeysHint: One key per line (ssh-ed25519, ssh-rsa, ecdsa-sha2-…).
vmForm.ciUserDataHint: Used as it is instead of the generated user-data (start with #cloud-config).
vmForm.ciVendorDataHint: Runs together with the generated user-data, for packages and runcmd.
vmForm.ciUserDataWarning: The user-data replaces the generated user-data; user, password and SSH keys are not used.
vmForm.windows11Hint: Filled in for Windows 11: q35, UEFI with Secure Boot, TPM 2.0, guest agent, 2 cores, 4096 MiB, SATA disks and e1000e interfaces, because the Windows installer has no VirtIO drivers. After installing the VirtIO drivers in Windows, switch the disks to virtio-blk and the interfaces to virtio for better speed.
vmForm.securityLive: TPM changes apply at the next restart. Secure Boot can only change while the VM is stopped.
vmForm.tpmHint: A virtual TPM (swtpm). Its state stays on the node the VM runs on and follows the VM. Windows 11 needs it.
vmForm.secureBootHint: UEFI firmware with Microsoft's keys enrolled. Only signed boot loaders start.
vmForm.tpmNodeOff: Node {{node}} cannot run a TPM (swtpm is missing or the node is too old).
vmForm.tpmNoNode: No node can run a TPM. Install swtpm on the nodes and restart orbivisor.
vmForm.secureBootNodeOff: Node {{node}} has no Secure Boot firmware (or is too old).
vmForm.secureBootNoNode: No node has Secure Boot firmware. Install the OVMF Secure Boot firmware on the nodes and restart orbivisor.
vmForm.secureBootRunning: Stop the VM to change Secure Boot.
vmForm.secureBootReset: The VM already has UEFI variables. Change Secure Boot with "Reset firmware" on the VM page.
vmForm.guestAgentHint: Shows the guest's addresses and OS, shuts down cleanly and freezes file systems for snapshots. Install qemu-guest-agent in the guest.
vmForm.guestAgentLive: Adding or removing the agent channel applies at the next restart. The other settings apply right away.
vmForm.agentFreeze: Freeze file systems for snapshots and backups
vmForm.agentFreezeHint: Asks the guest to flush and freeze its file systems so disk snapshots, backups and replicas are consistent.
vmForm.agentShutdownAgent: Through the guest agent, then ACPI

console.failed: Disconnected. The VM may have stopped or the console is not available.
console.pasteDenied: The browser did not allow reading the clipboard.
console.pasteTruncated: Only the first {{count}} characters were typed.
console.hint: Click the screen to type into the VM. Click outside it to release the keyboard.
console.forbidden: You do not have permission to use the console.

dashboard.mixedVersions: Nodes run different Orbivisor versions ({{versions}}). Finish the upgrade on every node.

subscription.invalid: The subscription key does not match this build.
subscription.over_limit: The cluster has {{used}} nodes, but the subscription covers {{limit}}.

settings.channelHint: Every node gets Orbivisor packages from this channel. Testing gets new versions before stable.
settings.adminOnly: Only administrators can change the settings.

errors.busy: Another settings change is in progress. Try again.

subscription.title: Subscription
subscription.keyHint: Paste the key you received. It starts with opl1.
subscription.removeDescription: The cluster will have no subscription. Nodes on the enterprise channel stop getting updates.

telemetry.title: Telemetry
telemetry.intro: When on, the leader sends a usage report once a day: counts and versions only, without names, addresses or keys.
telemetry.buildDefault: Not set (the build's default endpoint is used if it has one)
telemetry.endpointHint: An https:// address. Leave it empty to use the build default.
telemetry.previewDescription: This is the report the cluster would send now. Nothing else is sent.

shutdown.title: HA VMs on host shutdown

hint.conditional: Freeze on reboot, fail over on power off.
hint.freeze: Turn the node's HA VMs off and start them on the same node when it comes back. HA does not move them meanwhile.
hint.failover: Turn the node's HA VMs off; HA starts them on other nodes after the usual recovery wait.
hint.migrate: Live-migrate the node's VMs away first (node drain, up to 10 minutes), then fail over the remaining HA VMs.

shutdown.note: Applies only when the host reboots or powers off. Stopping or upgrading orbivisord leaves the VMs running.

ha.title: HA capacity
ha.reserveHint: Memory of HA-capable nodes kept free for recovery. Starting an HA VM that would use it is refused. All running VMs count; migrations are not checked.
ha.concurrencyHint: How many HA VMs the leader starts at once on one node during recovery (1–32, default 4).

prometheus.title: Prometheus
prometheus.intro: Each node can serve its metrics in the Prometheus text format. Scrape every node: each one exports only its own node, VMs and pools, plus the cluster values.
prometheus.auth: Prometheus signs in with an API token of a viewer or higher. Trust the cluster CA for HTTPS.

settings.notificationsIntro: Where alert rules send notifications: mail servers and webhooks (Slack, Teams, ntfy, Gotify).

audit.adminOnly: Only administrators can read the audit log.
audit.refreshFailed: Could not read the audit log again. {{error}}
audit.empty: No audit entries in this range.
audit.unreachable: No audit entries from these nodes (unreachable): {{nodes}}
audit.disabled: The audit log is turned off on these nodes: {{nodes}}
audit.truncated: Showing the newest {{count}} entries. More match; narrow the range or the filters.

haGroups.pageHint: HA VMs in a group are placed and recovered on the group's nodes, higher priority first. When a higher-priority node comes back, a running VM moves back to it by live migration unless the group has No failback.
haGroups.deleteDescription: VMs must not use the group. Placed VMs stay where they are.
haGroups.dialogDescription: HA VMs choose a group in their HA settings. VMs that are already placed are not moved.
haGroups.nodesHint: Priority from 0 to 1000; higher goes first. Empty means 0.
haGroups.restrictedHint: Never place the VMs outside the group. If no group node can take a VM, HA leaves it off and shows why.
haGroups.nofailbackHint: Do not move VMs back when a higher-priority node comes back.

errors.exists: An HA group with this name already exists.
errors.priority: Priorities are whole numbers from 0 to 1000.

haChecks.pageHint: Every node checks these links, ping targets and storage pool paths every 5 seconds and sends the results with its lease. When a check fails on a node for longer than the grace time, the leader reacts as set below. If a check fails on most of the nodes reporting it, the leader treats it as a shared failure and only warns. Only HA VMs are moved.
haChecks.autoNote: Each node also checks its cluster links by itself (cluster-link-1, cluster-link-2 …). Those checks only warn and are shown with the node.
haChecks.graceHint: How long the check must fail before the leader reacts: 10 to 600 seconds (at least two check rounds). Empty means 10.
haChecks.overridesHint: A different target on some nodes, such as another interface name. Other nodes use the target above.

roleHint.management: The node's management network. Failing it only warns unless you choose power-off fencing.
roleHint.storage: The path to shared storage. VMs with disks on it are affected; by default they are restarted on another node, since a VM with stuck disk I/O cannot be live migrated.
roleHint.vm: A network VMs use. VMs with NICs on the bridges behind the interface are affected; by default they are live migrated.

kindHint.link: Passes while the interface has a link. For a bond, losing some ports only shows as degraded; losing all fails.
kindHint.ping: Pings each address once (2 seconds); passes when at least Need addresses answer. Via picks the interface (Linux only).
kindHint.pool: Reads a small file on the pool (NFS, shared directory), checks the iSCSI sessions and multipath paths (shared LVM) or asks the Ceph OSDs (RBD).

haChecks.deleteDescription: Nodes stop running the check. VMs already moved stay where they are.
haChecks.dialogDescription: All nodes in the cluster must run a version that knows HA checks.

errors.exists: An HA check with this name already exists.
errors.reserved: Names starting with cluster-link- are for the nodes' own cluster link checks.
errors.iface: Use an interface name of 1–15 characters without /, : or spaces.
errors.address: Use IPv4 or IPv6 addresses, separated by commas.
errors.need: Need is a whole number from 1 to the number of addresses.
errors.poolRole: Pool checks need the storage role.
errors.action: This role does not allow that reaction.
errors.grace: Grace is a whole number of seconds from 10 to 600.
errors.overrideNode: Choose the node for this override.

placementRules.pageHint: Rules for where VMs run, for all VMs. Hard rules must hold: creating, starting or migrating a VM that would break one is refused. Soft rules are kept when possible. The leader shows broken rules on each VM. VMs already placed are not moved when you add a rule.
placementRules.dialogDescription: Hard rules that contradict each other are refused. Node labels (such as zone=rack-a) can choose nodes.

kinds.soft-node-anti-affinity: Away from these nodes if possible

kindHint.affinity: The VMs always run on one node and move together; one of them alone cannot be migrated.
kindHint.anti-affinity: No two of the VMs run on the same node.
kindHint.soft-affinity: Prefers one node for the VMs; each VM elsewhere adds the weight.
kindHint.soft-anti-affinity: Prefers different nodes; each other VM on the same node adds the weight.
kindHint.node-affinity: The VMs run only on the chosen nodes.
kindHint.node-anti-affinity: The VMs never run on the chosen nodes.
kindHint.soft-node-affinity: Prefers the chosen nodes; another node adds the weight.
kindHint.soft-node-anti-affinity: Avoids the chosen nodes; a chosen node adds the weight.

placementRules.vmNamesHint: Separate names with commas. VMs you create later may be named here.
placementRules.vmTagHint: KEY=VALUE, such as app=web. Every VM with this label.
placementRules.nodeTagHint: KEY=VALUE, such as zone=rack-a. Set node labels on the Nodes page.
placementRules.weightHint: From 1 to 100. Empty means 50. A higher weight matters more.
placementRules.haMayViolate: HA recovery may break this rule
placementRules.haMayViolateHint: If HA can recover a VM only by breaking the rule, it starts the VM anyway and shows the broken rule. Otherwise the VM stays off.

errors.exists: A placement rule with this name already exists.
errors.vmNames: Use valid VM names, each once.

placement.pageHint: Every node sends a load summary (CPU over 1 and 5 minutes, memory) with its lease every 5 seconds. Starting VMs, HA recovery and node draining choose the node with the best score. Every 5 minutes the balancer looks at how uneven the nodes are and recommends, or makes, live migrations.

modeHint.off: The balancer does nothing. Placement still uses load scores.
modeHint.recommend: The balancer only recommends moves; apply them yourself.
modeHint.auto: The balancer starts up to two live migrations at a time by itself.

policyHint.pack: Fill busy nodes first, keeping others free. The balancer only fixes broken hard rules.

placement.thresholdHint: From 1 to 50 percent. The balancer starts moving VMs when the imbalance (the mean of the CPU and memory spread across nodes) is above this and goes on until it is below 0.8 times this. A node whose CPU or memory use is more than twice this above the average is relieved even when the imbalance is lower.

pausedReasons.pack: The policy is pack, so the balancer does not move VMs for balance.
pausedReasons.fewNodes: Fewer than two nodes have a recent load summary.

placement.noSummaryHint: No recent load summary: the score uses the other nodes' mean CPU and allocated memory.

ceph.pageHint: A Ceph cluster that Orbivisor installs and runs on the cluster nodes: monitors, managers and OSDs on whole disks, with RBD pools registered as storage pools. To use an existing Ceph cluster, create a Ceph RBD storage pool instead.
ceph.none: No Ceph cluster is set up. An administrator can set one up here.
ceph.settingUp: Ceph is being set up on {{node}}.
ceph.notReady: Setting up Ceph did not finish.
ceph.retryElsewhere: {{node}} is offline; set Ceph up on
ceph.stale: This is the Ceph status read at {{time}}. It cannot be read now: {{error}}
ceph.osds: OSDs: {{up}} up, {{in}} in, {{total}} total on {{hosts}} hosts

mon.addDescription: The node installs the Ceph packages and joins the monitor quorum. Three monitors on different nodes keep Ceph running when one node is down.
mon.limit: The Ceph cluster already has {{n}} monitors, the most it can have here.
mon.even: An odd number of monitors (3 or 5) keeps quorum best.

mgr.addDescription: The node installs the Ceph packages and runs a standby manager that takes over when the active one stops.

osd.addDescription: The node installs the Ceph packages and makes an OSD (BlueStore on LVM) on the whole disk.
osd.typeDevice: Type {{device}} to erase all data on it
osd.wipeWarning: The disk is not empty: {{reasons}}. Everything on it is erased.

pool.createDescription: Creates an RBD pool in Ceph and registers it as a shared storage pool that every node uses through the managed client configuration.
pool.cephPoolHint: Leave empty to use the storage pool name.
pool.sizeHint: {{hosts}} hosts have OSDs that are up. Each copy is kept on a different host.
pool.sizeOne: Size 1 keeps a single copy: data is lost when that disk fails.
pool.sizeTwo: Size 2 can lose data when one copy is down; 3 is recommended.
pool.singleConfirm: I understand that there is no redundancy

clients.title: Install Ceph client packages
clients.description: Nodes without Ceph daemons need ceph-common and QEMU's rbd driver (qemu-block-extra) to use the Ceph pools. Their client configuration is already written.
clients.none: Every online node already runs Ceph daemons or is a witness.

wizard.title: Set up Ceph
wizard.networkHint: The first monitor and manager run on this node. Nodes need the same Ceph release, synchronised clocks (NTP) and open ports 3300, 6789 and 6800-7300/tcp.
wizard.publicHint: The network of monitors and clients (CIDR). Filled in from the node's address; leave empty to let the server choose it the same way.
wizard.clusterHint: Optional separate network for OSD replication (CIDR).
wizard.monsHint: Add monitors on two more nodes (three are recommended), one at a time. You can skip this.
wizard.osdsHint: Add OSDs on whole disks of the nodes. Disks that are not empty must be erased; disks in use cannot be chosen.
wizard.poolHint: Create a Ceph pool and register it as a storage pool. Add OSDs first.
wizard.clientsHint: Optionally install the Ceph client packages on nodes without Ceph daemons so that their VMs can use the pools.

downloads.title: Download a disk image
downloads.description: A node that can use the pool downloads the file, so it must reach the URL (set HTTPS_PROXY on the nodes for a proxy). Give the SHA-256 checksum to check the file.
downloads.sha256Hint: 64 hex digits from the publisher's checksum file.

errors.url: Enter an http or https URL.

isos.note: ISO images are kept in directory and NFS pools and can be in the CD-ROM drives of many VMs at once. An ISO in a node-local pool keeps its VMs on that node.

reason.inUse: Eject it from the VMs first.

isos.deleteDescription: The image file is deleted. Snapshots whose VM had it in a drive keep it from being deleted.

templates.note: A template is a VM that cannot be started. Deploying makes its disks linked clones (thin copies sharing the base) in the same pool, or full copies where the pool cannot hold linked clones.
templates.empty: No templates. Choose "Convert to template" in a stopped VM's menu or download one from the image library.
templates.revertDescription: Releases the base snapshots and makes it an ordinary VM. Not possible while linked clones remain.
templates.deleteDescription: Converts it back to a VM and deletes it. The disk volumes are kept.
templates.convertDescription: A template cannot be started and its disks cannot be changed. Deploy VMs from it; convert it back while it has no linked clones.
templates.deployDescription: Empty fields keep the template's values. The deploy task runs on the template's node.
templates.deployStopped: Stopped: could not deploy {{name}} ({{rest}} more not deployed): {{error}}
templates.name: New VM name
templates.nameHint: For several VMs {n} becomes a number (e.g. web-{n}).

modeHint.auto: Disks that cannot be linked are copied in full, with a warning.
modeHint.linked: Refused if any disk cannot be a linked clone.
modeHint.full: Makes disks independent of the base (takes longer).

templates.nodeHint: The node must reach the disks (a shared pool or its own local pool).
templates.diskNotLinkable: Cannot be linked — full copy (other pool, or the pool cannot hold linked clones)
templates.ciNote: With cloud-init on, only the fields you fill change the template's settings. For several VMs leave the host name empty (the VM name is used).

reason.notStopped: Only a stopped VM can become a template.
reason.clonesUnknown: Cannot tell whether linked clones exist.
reason.inUse: Linked clones remain. Delete or flatten them first.

errors.first: Enter a whole number of 0 or more.
errors.pattern: Put {n} in the name to deploy several VMs.
errors.notLinkable: Some disks cannot be linked clones.
errors.memory: Enter a whole number of at least 64 MiB.
errors.hostname: Several VMs cannot share one host name. Leave it empty to use the VM names.
errors.staticIp: Several VMs cannot share one static address.

images.note: Well-known cloud images. The downloading node checks each image against the publisher's checksum file and can make a template from the disk right away.
images.removeDescription: Removes it from the list only. Downloaded volumes and templates are kept.
images.downloadDescription: A node that can use the pool downloads the image and its checksum file, so it must reach the publisher.
images.addDescription: An image entry for this cluster only. Use the same id for each architecture; built-in ids cannot be used.
images.idHint: Lowercase letters, digits, ., _ and -, up to 63 (e.g. myos-1.0).
images.title: Title

errors.size: Smaller than the image's disk size.
errors.id: Start with a lowercase letter or digit and use only lowercase letters, digits, ., _ and - (up to 63).

metrics.title: Metrics
metrics.approxNote: ≈ Percentiles over this range are computed from averages and underestimate short peaks.
metrics.witness: Witness nodes keep no metrics history.
metrics.noNodeHistory: No node has metrics history yet.
metrics.noVms: No VM history in this range.

alerts.unreachable: These nodes did not answer, so their alerts are missing: {{nodes}}.
alerts.unsupported: These nodes run an older version without alerts: {{nodes}}.

history.subject: Subject
history.empty: No notifications were sent in this period.
history.truncated: Only the newest notifications are shown.

rules.deleteDescription: Its active alerts disappear without a notification.
rules.unitHint: Units: CPU and other % values in percent, memory in MiB, disk and network in bytes per second.
rules.opsHint: For example vm-start, vm-migrate. Leave empty for every task.
rules.forSecsHint: The condition must hold this long before it notifies (0 to 86400).
rules.noTargets: There are no notification targets. Create one first.
rules.repeatSecsHint: Notify again while the alert lasts. 0 sends once; otherwise 60 to 604800.
rules.namesHint: Names separated by commas. Leave empty for all.

errors.name: Use 1-63 lowercase letters, digits and '-', not starting or ending with '-'.
errors.taken: That name is already in use.
errors.repeatSecs: Enter 0, or whole seconds from 60 to 604800.

targets.adminOnly: Only administrators can manage notification targets.
targets.pageHint: Alert rules send to these targets by name. Passwords, tokens, header values and webhook URL paths are never shown again.
targets.deleteDescription: Rules that still use it must be changed first.
targets.formDescription: Secrets you leave empty keep their saved values.
targets.userHint: Leave empty to send without signing in.
targets.secretSaved: A value is saved. Leave empty to keep it.
targets.toHint: Up to 20 addresses separated by commas.
targets.urlSaved: The path and query are hidden. Leave the URL as it is to keep it.
targets.urlHint: http:// or https:// address that receives a POST.
targets.caPemHint: Only trust this CA. Leave empty to use the system CAs.

errors.name: Use 1-63 lowercase letters, digits and '-', not starting or ending with '-'.
errors.taken: That name is already in use.
errors.passwordAgain: The server, port, user or TLS changed. Enter the password again or remove it.
errors.url: Enter an http:// or https:// URL.
errors.tokenUnused: Only ntfy and Gotify use a token.
errors.tokenAgain: The URL or CA changed. Enter the token again or remove it.
errors.header: Enter a name and value for each new header.
errors.headersAgain: The URL or CA changed. Enter the header values again or remove them.
